title: streaming: handle client cancel/disconnect + reconnect/resume and server timeout improvements
author: Jordan Patel
description: Motivation: customer workloads and internal canaries showed two classes of streaming failures: (1) clients abruptly cancelling or disconnecting without a clean close event, which left server-side streams and KV cache entries in an indeterminate state and increased GPU memory retention; (2) reconnect/resume semantics were inconsistent between Redwood's streaming API and the OpenAI-compat adapter, causing duplicate tokens or stuck streams when clients attempted to resume using last_event_id/offset. This PR implements end-to-end streaming lifecycle controls: improved client-cancel propagation, deterministic disconnect cleanup, reconnect/resume protocol with resume tokens, and safer server-side timeouts. Summary of changes: 1) runtime/streaming_manager: add explicit client-cancel signal handling and a two-phase shutdown for in-flight streams. On client cancel we now: (a) mark stream as CancelRequested, (b) attempt cooperative cancellation of model generation with a bounded grace period (configurable via STREAM_CANCEL_GRACE_MS), (c) fallback to forced termination if the model team kernels do not respond within the grace window. This prevents indefinite KV cache pinning and frees GPU resources. 2) runtime/kv_cache: add reference counting and GC hooks triggered by final stream states (Completed/Cancelled/Expired) to ensure cache entries are evicted deterministically even if the TCP connection drops mid-stream. 3) api/compat/openai_stream_adapter: implement resume token exchange in the OpenAI compatibility layer. When a client reconnects with a resume_token the adapter validates offsets against server-side stream checkpoints and rewinds/fast-forwards the stream to the next unapplied token to avoid duplicates. 4) api/gateway: enrich HTTP/WS close codes and add server-initiated close with a structured JSON body to signal reasons (timeout, cancel, internal_error) and optional resume_token when applicable. 5) sdk/typescript stream client: expose reconnect/resume helper utilities and add backoff/retry hooks that honor resume_token semantics. 6) tests: unit + integration + two new e2e scenarios that reproduce abrupt client TCP disconnect and reconnect-with-resume flows. 7) config: add STREAM_CANCEL_GRACE_MS and STREAM_RESUME_VALID_WINDOW_MS feature flags with sane defaults and observability hooks. Behavioral notes and compatibility: - Backwards-compatible: existing clients that do not send resume_token continue to work; they will receive a fresh stream and previous partial outputs are not re-applied. - OpenAI-compat: adapter maps OpenAI-style last_event_id to resume_token and validates offsets; this prevents both duplication and loss. - Timeouts: server-side stream idle timeout bumped to 2 minutes by default but now configurable per-route; we emit metrics for timeout triggers and provide a recovery path that includes a resume_token in the timeout body so well-behaved clients can reconnect and continue. Tests and validation: - Added unit tests for cancel propagation and KV cache GC. - Integration tests simulate abrupt TCP close during bursty token generation and assert no leaked GPU allocations after GC hook executes. - E2E tests run against the OpenAI-compat adapter to validate resume semantics and deduplication. Rollout plan and safety: - Feature gated behind STREAM_LIFECYCLE_V1; default enabled for internal canaries and 10% of hosted traffic for one week. - Canary metrics tracked: stream_duration, cancelled_count, forced_terminations, kv_cache_evictions, resume_success_rate. - If perf regressions appear, flag to revert is adding STREAM_LIFECYCLE_V1=false and rolling back the gateway adapter. Related: links to Linear tasks ENG-1284 (stream lifecycle) and ENG-1302 (openai compat resume); incident SUP-4421 was used to reproduce the issue. See release_notes for user-facing details.

release_notes: Users: Streaming connections now support reconnect/resume using resume_token. Clients that wish to resume should persist the resume_token received on disconnect or timeout and pass it when reconnecting. Server-side behavior: more deterministic cleanup on client cancel/disconnect, reduced GPU memory leaks, and improved deduplication for resumed streams. Admins: feature gates STREAM_LIFECYCLE_V1, STREAM_CANCEL_GRACE_MS, STREAM_RESUME_VALID_WINDOW_MS.
notes_for_operations: If resume-related metric errors spike, temporarily disable STREAM_LIFECYCLE_V1 and roll back gateway adapter; monitor kv_cache_evictions and forced_terminations. A hotfix branch exists: hotfix/streaming-rollforward-95321.
additional_context: This PR was driven by a SUP-4421 customer report and internal canaries that reproduced stuck streams under high interrupt rates. The approach favors deterministic resource reclamation and minimal duplication for resumed clients. We coordinated changes with model runtime owners to ensure the bounded cooperative cancellation path does not abort in-kernel state unexpectedly. Observability hooks were added to trace resume_token lifecycle.
